claim_scope: The q=5 degree-four Tate-duplication map has Julia set the folded Tate skeleton, preperiodic indifferent Fatou components, and finitely many forward SET images of every conventional nondegenerate positive-radius open or closed Berkovich disk, including projective-coordinate disks and irrational-radius disks; not radius-zero/generalized singleton sets or Gauss points viewed as disk substitutes.
claim_type: single-map Fatou classification and finite set-image orbits for every conventional positive-radius Berkovich disk
limitations: Disk means a conventional nondegenerate positive-radius open or closed Berkovich subset, including irrational radii and projective-coordinate disks; not its Gauss point or radius-zero/generalized singleton. Uses established Julia-segment, locally-compact tame no-wandering, periodic-component and typeII residue-map theory. No formal proof or external expert attestation is claimed; original external channel values remain recorded in VERIFICATION.md. No statement for wild residue characteristic or higher-rank fields.
priority_comparison: Julia segment and folded doubling: standard Tate-Lattes geometry already described in Benedetto2010 Project2(d-f), not a new q=5 fact.
No wandering Fatou components: direct specialization of the published locally-compact no-wild-recurrence theorem, with Q5 and degree4<5 checking every hypothesis.
Indifference: standard Lattes periodic multipliers \( \pm2^n,4^n \) plus the established periodic-component classification; no unsupported attracting-critical rule needed.
Arbitrary Fatou subdisks: published degree-one disk similarity/isometry combined with elementary compactness in a finite extension; no new exact datum or unresolved parameter.
Julia-meeting disks: elementary full-branch tent exactness plus published nonconstant typeII tangent-map surjectivity and complete Fatou-direction images.
Endpoint/irrational boundary cases: endpoint direction bookkeeping and the same tent/tangent arguments; infinite Gauss-point orbits do not produce new wandering disk subsets.

Exact rational map and torsion ledger: substitution into the standard Tate coefficients and Weierstrass formula, and standard involution torsion count \((4^n+4)/2\). Numerical q=5 fixes no independently unknown invariant.
proof_outline: Known Tate-Lattes Julia geometry gives J(L)=Sigma and total invariance. L is defined over the complete locally compact field Q5; degree4<residue characteristic5 makes every local degree tame and rules out wild recurrent Julia critical points. Benedetto lecture Theorem7.20/survey Theorem17.4 therefore makes every Fatou component preperiodic. Periodic-point multipliers \( \pm2^n \) and \(4^n\) are units; survey Theorem17.2 makes every periodic component degree1 and indifferent.

For any positive-radius disk disjoint from Sigma, take its eventual image D' inside a periodic indifferent component U, normalize U over a finite extension to the unit disk, and take its return f. Propositions3.14/3.15 give an isometry and analytic inverse. Choose an algebraic center b in D' and a finite extension F containing b and f's coefficients. Its center orbit stays in compact F intersect U; there are finitely many fixed-positive-radius ultrametric ball classes. Thus the subdisk orbit is finite. Propositions3.28/6.13 handle disk images; for a closed irrational disk add its typeIII boundary using density, continuity and compactness.

For a disk meeting a positive Julia interval choose a strictly interior interval I avoiding the omitted-direction attachment. An entire full monotonicity branch of T^N lies inside I for large N, so T^N(I)=Sigma. All off-skeleton components attached inside I lie wholly in D. Each target off-skeleton component attached at typeII eta has a typeII tent preimage xi in I. Theorem6.12 gives a nonconstant surjective residue tangent map. A skeletal source germ maps skeletal; hence an off-skeleton target direction has an off-skeleton preimage. That Fatou direction is not a surplus direction and maps its whole component onto the target. Thus L^N(D)=P1an.

A closed disk touching Sigma at only its boundary must be at a skeleton endpoint. It contains the endpoint plus ALL off-skeleton directions there, not merely the closure of one open Fatou component. Theorem6.12 and total invariance give L(B_xi)=B_{L(xi)}. The tent endpoints go1/2 to0 to0, giving finite set-image orbits.

In the standard Tate equation y^2+xy=x^3+a4*x+a6, a4=-5*sum k^3*5^k/(1-5^k), a6=-(1/12)*sum(7*k^5+5*k^3)*5^k/(1-5^k). The Weierstrass formula gives L(X)=(X^4-2*a4*X^2-8*a6*X+a4^2-a6)/(4*X^3+X^2+4*a4*X+4*a6). Silverman C.14's coordinate series yields Sigma={zeta(0,5^-s):0<=s<=1/2}. For irrational alpha, the typeIII boundary orbit is infinite but D_alpha intersect Sigma=[alpha,1/2] (open counterpart omits alpha); the whole disk therefore eventually maps onto P1an, not a target counterexample.

The original unrestricted attracting-critical lemma is genuinely false: lecture Remark7.18 supplies z^5 with attracting component D_Ber(1,1) and no critical point attracted to1. Proposition7.16 requires a return degree not divisible by the residue characteristic. This repairs a proof defect only; it is NOT a counterexample to the target map. Target component-return degrees are products of1..4, prime to5, or use the direct unit multipliers instead.
provenance: Mathematical reassessment preserves the original arbitrary-disk subset scope and replaces a false unrestricted attracting-critical lemma. The concrete z^5 primary counterexample demonstrates a general proof defect only, not falsehood of the target. Complete final C PASS/O FAIL/V FAIL: the full result is routinely implied by established theory, so the repaired proof is not a new accepted finding.
